criteria.expectation: Report identifies that the icon-only buttons in CartRow.swift (minus, plus, remove) use custom image assets (Image("ic_minus"/"ic_plus"/"ic_remove")) with no accessibilityLabel (or any text label), so VoiceOver has no meaningful name for them.
Cites CartRow.swift with line numbers or quoted code for at least the three buttons, and notes that other elements (Text names/prices, Pay now button) are fine because they have text.

Recommends adding concise localized accessibility labels to the buttons (e.g. decrease/increase quantity, remove item, ideally including the item name for remove), optionally with the quantity as value, and adding the strings to Localizable.xcstrings.

Does not claim a definitive exact VoiceOver announcement (e.g. says 'will read X') without hedging; frames the result as likely/unlabelled based on source, noting that custom assets do not get an automatic SF Symbol description.

Explicitly states that this was a source review and that VoiceOver behavior, Accessibility Inspector results, asset catalog contents/asset-level labels, and Dynamic Type rendering were not run or verified.
Does not present Dynamic Type clipping or fixed-height problems as confirmed defects (the code uses minHeight and no fixed heights); any such mention is hedged or labeled as unverified.
Report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any files in the input directory; fixes are described as suggestions only.

Does not report missing accessibility labels on the minus/plus/remove buttons (or any other confirmed VoiceOver/Dynamic Type defect) as a confirmed finding; acknowledges the buttons have accessibilityLabel in CartRow.swift.

States that VoiceOver output, Accessibility Inspector, asset catalog contents, localization of the new strings in other languages, and Dynamic Type rendering were not run/verified in this source-only review.

Does not recommend a substantial rewrite or demand changes as required; any extra suggestions (e.g. grouping row elements, adjustableAction stepper, xcstrings translator comments, .accessibilityElement(children:)) are explicitly labeled optional, minor or low priority.
Supports its conclusion with specific file/line references (e.g. the accessibilityLabel modifiers in CartRow.swift, minHeight usage rather than fixed heights).
Report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any files in the input directory.
